extracted.intended_audience: meta-researchers, journal editors, and researchers analysing peer review reports
extracted.subtask_description: Quantitative linguistic analysis of peer review reports using word counts, LIWC-derived dimensions (analytical tone, clout, authenticity, moral foundations), and multiple sentiment-scoring tools, stratified by reviewer gender, review model, recommendation, and research area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Word count (mean and 95% confidence interval) of peer review reports across groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 1: Reports recommending accept (red) were consistently the shortest, and reports recommending major revisions (green) were consistently the longest. Supplementary file 1 provides summary data and mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical tone (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for analytical tone (mean percentages and 95% confidence interval) of peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 2A: Scores shown by research area and reviewer gender for single-blind review; Supplementary file 2 contains summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low LIWC analytical tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clout (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for clout (mean percentages and 95% confidence interval) of peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 2B: Reports recommending accept consistently had the most clout, and reports recommending reject consistently had the least clout. Supplementary file 3 contains summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low LIWC clout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for authenticity (mean percentages and 95% confidence interval) of peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 2C: Presented by area and reviewer gender under single-blind review; Supplementary file 4 provides summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low LIWC authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment — LIWC emotional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment scores returned by LIWC (emotional tone; mean percentage and 95% CI) for peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 3A: Used alongside SentimentR and Stanford CoreNLP to assess sentiment; Supplementary file 5 includes summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low LIWC emotional tone scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment — SentimentR score
rubrics_metrics.description: SentimentR mean score (and 95% CI) for peer review reports as an alternate sentiment measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 3B: Presented to compare with LIWC and Stanford CoreNLP sentiment outputs; Supplementary file 6 contains summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low SentimentR scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment — Stanford CoreNLP score
rubrics_metrics.description: Stanford CoreNLP sentiment mean score (and 95% CI) for peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 3C: Used in parallel with LIWC and SentimentR; Supplementary file 7 provides summary data, mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals, and examples of reports with high and low CoreNLP sentiment scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: General morality (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for general morality (mean percentage on a log scale) in peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4: Reports recommending accept consistently had the highest scores for general morality. Supplementary file 8 lists the ten most frequent words found in peer review reports for general morality and the five moral foundation variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation — care/harm (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for the care/harm moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4—figure supplement 1: Care/harm is presented as one of the five moral foundation variables; Supplementary file 8 lists frequent words associated with this variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation — fairness/cheating (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for the fairness/cheating moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4—figure supplement 2: One of five moral foundations analysed; Supplementary file 8 lists frequent words associated with this variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation — loyalty/betrayal (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for the loyalty/betrayal moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4—figure supplement 3: One of five moral foundations analysed; Supplementary file 8 lists frequent words associated with this variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation — authority/subversion (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for the authority/subversion moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4—figure supplement 4: One of five moral foundations analysed; Supplementary file 8 lists frequent words associated with this variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral foundation — sanctity/degradation (LIWC)
rubrics_metrics.description: LIWC score for the sanctity/degradation moral foundation (mean percentage on a log scale and 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4—figure supplement 5: One of five moral foundations analysed; Supplementary file 8 lists frequent words associated with this variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation category (review outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical recommendation given by the reviewer (e.g., accept, major revisions, reject) used as an outcome/stratification variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures repeatedly compare linguistic metrics across recommendation categories (notes: accept associated with shortest reports and highest clout/morality; major revisions associated with longest reports; reject with lowest clout).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer gender (stratification variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer self-reported gender (female vs male) used to stratify analyses of linguistic metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show left panels for female reviewers and right panels for male reviewers; all LIWC/sentiment/morality metrics are reported separately by gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review model (single-blind vs double-blind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review model (single-blind or double-blind) used to stratify analyses of report language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures present parallel analyses for single-blind (Figure 2, 3, 4 bottom panels) and double-blind (figure supplements); comparisons indicate patterns may differ by review anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research area (broad disciplinary grouping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad area of research of the reviewed manuscript — HMS (health and medical sciences), LS (life sciences), PS (physical sciences), SS&E (social sciences and economics) — used as grouping variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures display scores for the four broad research areas; comparisons across areas are central to the analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple tools and supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of multiple automated text-analysis tools (LIWC, SentimentR, Stanford CoreNLP) and reporting of summary data plus mixed model linear regression coefficients and residuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary files (1–8) provide the data, model coefficients, residuals, and examples of reports with extreme/high/low scores for each metric — indicating that robustness across tools and transparency of model outputs are part of the evaluative standard.
